questions.title: Review of Complements and the Cumulative Column - Find a complement, test whether a table is a probability distribution, and state what the cumulative column must do
Build the Cumulative Column - Add the chances in order and give the running total at x = 1, 2 and 3
Read Three Probabilities from a Cumulative Table - Convert more than, between and fewer than to inequalities, then subtract cumulative entries
Phrase to Inequality to Probability - Turn at most, at least, more than, fewer than, no more than and no fewer than into an inequality, then read the cumulative table
Quiz Cumulative Tail and Interval - Build F(2) from a five-row quiz table, then read at least 3 and between 2 and 3 inclusive
Quartiles from a Cumulative Table - Use the cut-off rule to find the first quartile and the third quartile
Cut-Offs from a Cumulative Table - Find the smallest value whose running total reaches 0.6 and 0.9
Row Versus Running Total - Diagnose a student who reads P(X = 2) as P(X <= 2), then give both values and the jump at x = 2
Mean and the Largest Chance - Compute the mean from a three-row table, then test the claim that the mean is the value with the largest chance
Missing Value to Cumulative Table - Fill the missing chance from sum-to-1, then read F(2)
Pre-FRQ Grade a Cumulative Reasoning - The scenario and grading checklist of the cumulative-table FRQ, but the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
